title: MWBM-MEDIA-LANG conformance test cases, version 1
description: The test cases every implementation of the Media Language & BCP 47 Policy (docs/standards/media-language-bcp47-policy.md) must pass for the profiles it implements. Each case lists the rule IDs it checks. The expected answers were worked out by hand from the policy text and cross-checked by an independent throwaway implementation before publication.
$comment: Master copy: MWBMPartners/MeedyaSuite-core. Other repositories keep an exact copy checked by scripts/media-lang/check_copies.py. Changing an expected answer is a MAJOR policy version change; adding cases is MINOR (see the policy's 'Changing this policy').

$schema.description: Relative path to this schema, so editors can validate the file.

policy.description: The policy these cases belong to.

policy_version.description: The policy version whose rules these cases test.

fixtures_version.description: Version of this case file. Tied to policy_version: a new MAJOR policy version always gets a new MAJOR fixtures version.

data_version.description: The reference data version (docs/standards/data/bcp47-language-data-v1.json) the canonicalisation and legacy-code answers were computed against. A registry refresh that changes an answer must bump this and the fixtures version together.

canonicalise.description: LANG-001 canonical form. Implementations call their canonicalise function on 'input'.

input.description: Raw value as it might arrive from a file, database or user.

expected.description: Canonical tag, or null when the input is malformed (LANG-026).

kind.description: ordinary = a normal langtag; grandfathered = a registry grandfathered tag with no replacement, kept as the registry spells it; privateuse = a tag starting 'x-'; malformed = not a well-formed tag.

note.description: Why this case exists, where that is not obvious.

legacy_three_letter.description: LANG-002: reading an old three-letter (ISO 639-2) field from a container or tag format.

input.description: The value found in the old field (e.g. 'ger', 'XXX', 'fre-ca').

expected.description: The canonical BCP 47 tag, or null for 'unrecognised' (the caller then stores 'und' and keeps the raw text).

posix_locale.description: LANG-004: converting an operating-system locale name.

input.description: A locale name such as 'en_US.UTF-8' or 'sr_RS@latin'.

expected.description: The canonical tag, or null when the locale names no language ('C', 'POSIX') or cannot be converted.

canonical_order.description: Part A stored order of a list of language-tagged items (LANG-010 to LANG-027).

description.description: What the case shows, in plain words.

id.description: Identifier used in 'expected'. When absent, the tag itself is the identifier.

tag.description: Raw language value; canonicalised by the implementation.

original.description: Structured 'original language' marker (LANG-010). Absent means false.

track_order.description: Part A stored order of container tracks (TRACK-050, TRACK-060).

description.description: What the case shows, in plain words.

presentation_order.description: Part B menu order (UI-020 to UI-050). Names and sorting keys are supplied in the case so the answer does not depend on the platform's locale data: the implementation's test harness MUST name groups with display_names and sort them by comparing collation_keys as plain strings, in place of real locale data.

subtitle_menu.description: UI-060: a subtitle menu is 'off' followed by the subtitle tracks in presentation order.

label.description: UI-070 menu labels built from structured data. Localised strings are supplied; the case checks the joining and role order.

type.description: Track type; decides which role order applies (TRACK-050).

roles.description: The track's roles, in any order; the label lists them in TRACK-050 order.

role_names.description: Localised word for each role present.

channels.description: Channel layout text for audio (e.g. '5.1'), or null.

expected.description: The label, parts joined with ' — ' (space, U+2014 em dash, space).

match.description: MATCH-010 to MATCH-040: strength of match between one preference and one candidate tag.

preference.description: The user's preferred tag (raw; canonicalised first).

candidate.description: The track or translation tag (raw; canonicalised first).

level.description: Match strength, best first: exact, general (candidate is a shorter form), specific (candidate is a longer form), related (same language, no script conflict), none.

distance.description: For general and specific: how many subtags were removed or added. 0 otherwise.

auto_select_audio.description: AUTO-020 audio selection. Harnesses MUST also run each case with the tracks in reverse order and get the same answer (AUTO-010).

description.description: What the case shows, in plain words.

auto_select_subtitle.description: AUTO-030 subtitle selection. Harnesses MUST also run each case with the tracks in reverse order and get the same answer (AUTO-010).

description.description: What the case shows, in plain words.

audio.description: Tag of the audio track already chosen, or null if there is none.

expected.description: Identifier of the subtitle track chosen, or null for none.

caseId.description: Stable case identifier. Never reused for a different case.

rules.description: Policy rule IDs this case checks.

role.description: Track role (TRACK-010). A track with no roles is the main programme (audio) or full subtitles.

preferences.description: The user's language preferences, highest priority first (raw tags; malformed ones are ignored).

audio_description.description: The user has asked for audio description (AUTO-040).

captions.description: The user has asked for SDH / captions (AUTO-040).

accessibility.description: Accessibility preferences. Absent keys mean false.

original.description: Structured original-language marker. Absent means false.

id.description: Track identifier; the final tie-break (AUTO-010), compared as a plain string in these cases.

description.description: What the case shows, in plain words.

selected.description: An item the user has selected. Present only to show that selection changes nothing (UI-050); the ordering function takes no selection input.

display_names.description: Localised name of each ordinary primary language present, keyed by primary language subtag.

collation_keys.description: Stand-in for the interface language's sorting rules: groups sort by comparing these keys as plain strings (then by primary subtag).

type.description: Item type; decides which role order and accessibility preference apply. Absent means a plain language item with no roles.

items.description: Items in file or database order.
